title: Can Rabbits Eat Mulberries?
description: It does not replace advice from a rabbit-savvy vet. If your rabbit stops eating, stops pooing, seems in pain or is suddenly unwell, contact a vet…
body:
<div class="wp-block-group alignfull">
<!--
RabbitCare.co.uk blog article block
Page: Can Rabbits Eat Mulberries?
How to use in WordPress:
1) Edit the blog page/post.
2) Add a "Custom HTML" block.
3) Replace the old article content with everything below.

Notes:
- No custom header/nav or footer included.
- Internal links use root-relative URLs.
- Uses the same visual style as the RabbitCare homepage and rabbit food guides.
-->

<section class="rcm-page alignfull" id="can-rabbits-eat-mulberries">
  <style>
    :root {
      --rc-cream: #fff9ef;
      --rc-cream-2: #f6ead8;
      --rc-sage: #7f9b72;
      --rc-sage-dark: #4e6b45;
      --rc-moss: #2f4a2e;
      --rc-brown: #8a6246;
      --rc-gold: #d7a64b;
      --rc-charcoal: #2d2d2b;
      --rc-muted: #6f6a61;
      --rc-white: #ffffff;
      --rc-danger: #9b3b2f;
      --rc-danger-soft: #fff0eb;
      --rc-shadow: 0 24px 70px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.16);
      --rc-radius-xl: 34px;
      --rc-radius-lg: 24px;
      --rc-radius-md: 16px;
      --rc-max: 1180px;
      --rc-font-heading: Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif;
      --rc-font-body: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
    }

    .rcm-page,
    .rcm-page * { box-sizing: border-box; }

    body,
    .wp-site-blocks,
    .entry-content,
    .wp-block-post-content,
    main { background: #fef4f0 !important; }

    body .wp-site-blocks,
    body .entry-content,
    body .wp-block-post-content,
    body main,
    body article,
    body .wp-block-group,
    body .wp-block-post-content > .wp-block-html {
      margin-top: 0 !important;
      padding-top: 0 !important;
      gap: 0 !important;
      row-gap: 0 !important;
    }

    body .entry-header,
    body .page-header,
    body .wp-block-post-title,
    body h1.wp-block-post-title,
    body .wp-block-post-featured-image { display: none !important; }

    body .wp-site-blocks > * + *,
    body .entry-content > * + *,
    body .wp-block-post-content > * + * { margin-block-start: 0 !important; }

    body .wp-block-html,
    body .entry-content > .wp-block-html,
    body .wp-block-post-content > .wp-block-html {
      margin-top: 0 !important;
      margin-bottom: 0 !important;
      padding-top: 0 !important;
      padding-bottom: 0 !important;
    }

    .rcm-page {
      position: relative;
      left: calc(50% + 20px);
      width: calc(100vw + 40px);
      max-width: none;
      margin: -120px 0 0 !important;
      padding: 0 !important;
      transform: translateX(-50%);
      color: var(--rc-charcoal);
      font-family: var(--rc-font-body);
      background:
        radial-gradient(circle at top left, rgba(215, 166, 75, 0.18), transparent 32rem),
        linear-gradient(180deg, var(--rc-cream) 0%, #fffdf8 46%, #fef4f0 100%);
      overflow-x: hidden;
      line-height: 1.68;
    }

    .rcm-page a { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; }

    .rcm-page a:focus-visible {
      outline: 3px solid rgba(215, 166, 75, 0.9);
      outline-offset: 4px;
      border-radius: 10px;
    }

    .rcm-wrap { width: min(var(--rc-max), calc(100% - 34px)); margin: 0 auto; }
    .rcm-narrow { width: min(920px, calc(100% - 34px)); margin: 0 auto; }

    .rcm-pill {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 8px;
      color: var(--rc-sage-dark);
      font-size: 0.84rem;
      font-weight: 900;
      letter-spacing: 0.04em;
      text-transform: uppercase;
    }

    .rcm-pill::before { content: "✦"; color: var(--rc-gold); }

    .rcm-btns {
      display: flex;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
      gap: 14px;
      align-items: center;
      margin-top: 30px;
    }

    .rcm-btn {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: center;
      min-height: 52px;
      padding: 14px 22px;
      border-radius: 999px;
      font-weight: 900;
      transition: transform 0.25s ease, box-shadow 0.25s ease, background 0.25s ease;
    }

    .rcm-btn:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); }

    .rcm-btn-primary {
      background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--rc-sage-dark), var(--rc-sage));
      color: #fff;
      box-shadow: 0 18px 38px rgba(79, 112, 70, 0.26);
    }

    .rcm-btn-secondary {
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.9);
      color: var(--rc-moss);
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.16);
      box-shadow: 0 12px 28px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.10);
    }

    .rcm-hero {
      padding: 0 0 42px;
      background:
        radial-gradient(circle at 80% 20%, rgba(127, 155, 114, 0.18), transparent 28rem),
        linear-gradient(180deg, #fff9ef 0%, rgba(255, 249, 239, 0) 100%);
    }

    .rcm-hero-image-wrap {
      width: 100%;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      background: #fff9ef;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .rcm-hero-cover { position: relative; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; }

    .rcm-hero-cover::after {
      content: "";
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      background:
        linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(31, 45, 27, 0.68), rgba(31, 45, 27, 0.24) 45%, rgba(31, 45, 27, 0.04)),
        linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18), transparent 45%, rgba(255, 249, 239, 0.12));
      pointer-events: none;
    }

    .rcm-hero-image {
      display: block;
      width: 100%;
      height: auto;
      object-fit: contain;
      object-position: center;
      background: #fff;
      animation: rcmFadeIn 0.9s ease both;
    }

    .rcm-hero-title-overlay {
      position: absolute;
      z-index: 2;
      left: max(24px, calc((100vw - var(--rc-max)) / 2));
      bottom: clamp(28px, 8vw, 96px);
      max-width: 720px;
      padding: clamp(20px, 4vw, 38px);
      color: #ffffff;
    }

    .rcm-hero-title-overlay .rcm-pill {
      color: #ffffff;
      text-shadow: 0 3px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35);
    }

    .rcm-hero-title-overlay h1 {
      margin: 12px 0 12px;
      font-family: var(--rc-font-heading);
      font-size: clamp(3rem, 7vw, 7rem);
      line-height: 0.88;
      letter-spacing: -0.065em;
      color: #ffffff;
      text-wrap: balance;
      text-shadow: 0 5px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.42);
    }

    .rcm-hero-title-overlay p {
      max-width: 560px;
      margin: 0;
      color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.94);
      font-size: clamp(1.05rem, 2vw, 1.35rem);
      font-weight: 700;
      text-shadow: 0 3px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.36);
    }

    .rcm-hero-content {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 1.05fr 0.95fr;
      gap: 34px;
      align-items: center;
      padding-top: 44px;
    }

    .rcm-breadcrumb {
      display: inline-flex;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 8px;
      margin-bottom: 18px;
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-size: 0.95rem;
      font-weight: 800;
    }

    .rcm-breadcrumb a { color: var(--rc-sage-dark); }

    .rcm-intro-heading {
      margin: 12px 0 16px;
      font-family: var(--rc-font-heading);
      font-size: clamp(2.2rem, 5vw, 4.4rem);
      line-height: 0.98;
      letter-spacing: -0.055em;
      color: var(--rc-charcoal);
      text-wrap: balance;
    }

    .rcm-hero-subtitle {
      max-width: 720px;
      margin: 0;
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-size: clamp(1.08rem, 2vw, 1.28rem);
    }

    .rcm-hero-card {
      padding: 28px;
      border-radius: 38px;
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.12);
      box-shadow: var(--rc-shadow);
      backdrop-filter: blur(18px);
    }

    .rcm-hero-card h2 {
      margin: 0 0 14px;
      color: var(--rc-moss);
      font-size: 1.35rem;
      line-height: 1.18;
    }

    .rcm-hero-card ul {
      display: grid;
      gap: 12px;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      list-style: none;
    }

    .rcm-hero-card li {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 32px 1fr;
      gap: 10px;
      align-items: start;
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-weight: 700;
    }

    .rcm-hero-card li::before {
      content: "✓";
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      width: 32px;
      height: 32px;
      border-radius: 50%;
      background: rgba(127, 155, 114, 0.14);
      color: var(--rc-sage-dark);
      font-weight: 900;
    }

    .rcm-quickbar { position: relative; z-index: 4; margin-top: 26px; }

    .rcm-quickbar-inner {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
      gap: 14px;
      padding: 16px;
      border-radius: var(--rc-radius-xl);
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.12);
      box-shadow: var(--rc-shadow);
      backdrop-filter: blur(18px);
    }

    .rcm-quick {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 62px 1fr;
      align-items: center;
      gap: 14px;
      min-height: 96px;
      padding: 18px;
      border-radius: 24px;
      background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fff, #fff8eb);
      transition: transform 0.25s ease, box-shadow 0.25s ease;
    }

    .rcm-quick:hover {
      transform: translateY(-5px);
      box-shadow: 0 16px 34px rgba(83, 61, 42, 0.14);
    }

    .rcm-quick-icon {
      width: 62px;
      height: 62px;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      font-size: 2.35rem;
      line-height: 1;
    }

    .rcm-quick strong {
      display: block;
      color: var(--rc-moss);
      line-height: 1.15;
      font-size: 1.02rem;
    }

    .rcm-quick span span {
      display: block;
      margin-top: 4px;
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-size: 0.9rem;
      line-height: 1.35;
    }

    .rcm-section { width: 100%; padding: 72px 0; position: relative; }

    .rcm-section-header {
      max-width: 780px;
      margin: 0 auto 32px;
      text-align: center;
    }

    .rcm-section h2,
    .rcm-final h2 {
      margin: 12px 0 12px;
      font-family: var(--rc-font-heading);
      font-size: clamp(2.2rem, 5vw, 4.6rem);
      line-height: 0.98;
      letter-spacing: -0.055em;
      color: var(--rc-charcoal);
      text-wrap: balance;
    }

    .rcm-section-header p {
      margin: 0 auto;
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-size: 1.08rem;
      max-width: 680px;
    }

    .rcm-article-layout {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 320px;
      gap: 28px;
      align-items: start;
    }

    .rcm-content { display: grid; gap: 24px; }

    .rcm-panel {
      position: relative;
      padding: clamp(24px, 4vw, 38px);
      border-radius: var(--rc-radius-xl);
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.86);
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.12);
      box-shadow: 0 18px 48px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.10);
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .rcm-panel::after {
      content: "";
      position: absolute;
      width: 190px;
      height: 190px;
      right: -82px;
      top: -92px;
      border-radius: 50%;
      background: rgba(127, 155, 114, 0.10);
      pointer-events: none;
    }

    .rcm-panel > * { position: relative; z-index: 1; }
    .rcm-panel h2 { margin-top: 0; }

    .rcm-panel h3 {
      margin: 0 0 10px;
      color: var(--rc-moss);
      font-size: 1.45rem;
      line-height: 1.2;
    }

    .rcm-panel p {
      margin: 0 0 16px;
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-size: 1.03rem;
    }

    .rcm-panel p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }

    .rcm-list {
      display: grid;
      gap: 12px;
      margin: 22px 0 0;
      padding: 0;
      list-style: none;
    }

    .rcm-list li {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 38px 1fr;
      gap: 12px;
      align-items: start;
      padding: 15px;
      border-radius: 20px;
      background: rgba(255, 249, 239, 0.9);
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.10);
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-weight: 700;
    }

    .rcm-list li::before {
      content: "✓";
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      width: 38px;
      height: 38px;
      border-radius: 50%;
      background: rgba(127, 155, 114, 0.14);
      color: var(--rc-sage-dark);
      font-weight: 900;
    }

    .rcm-treat-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr));
      gap: 18px;
      margin-top: 28px;
    }

    .rcm-treat-card {
      padding: 24px;
      border-radius: var(--rc-radius-xl);
      background: #ffffff;
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.12);
      box-shadow: 0 16px 42px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.10);
      transition: transform 0.25s ease, box-shadow 0.25s ease;
    }

    .rcm-treat-card:hover {
      transform: translateY(-6px);
      box-shadow: 0 24px 58px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.15);
    }

    .rcm-treat-card b {
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      width: 54px;
      height: 54px;
      margin-bottom: 18px;
      border-radius: 22px;
      background: rgba(127, 155, 114, 0.14);
      color: var(--rc-sage-dark);
      font-size: 1.2rem;
    }

    .rcm-treat-card h3 { margin: 0 0 8px; color: var(--rc-moss); font-size: 1.22rem; }
    .rcm-treat-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--rc-muted); }

    .rcm-warning {
      padding: 68px 0;
      background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 240, 235, 0.56), rgba(255, 255, 255, 0));
    }

    .rcm-warning-card {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 0.9fr 1.1fr;
      gap: 28px;
      align-items: center;
      padding: clamp(24px, 5vw, 44px);
      border-radius: 42px;
      background: #ffffff;
      border: 2px solid rgba(155, 59, 47, 0.16);
      box-shadow: var(--rc-shadow);
    }

    .rcm-warning-card h2 { color: var(--rc-danger); }

    .rcm-warning-card p {
      margin: 0;
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      font-size: 1.06rem;
    }

    .rcm-warning-list {
      display: grid;
      gap: 12px;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      list-style: none;
    }

    .rcm-warning-list li {
      padding: 18px;
      border-radius: 20px;
      background: var(--rc-danger-soft);
      color: #4a2823;
      font-weight: 800;
    }

    .rcm-warning-list strong {
      display: block;
      margin-bottom: 4px;
      color: var(--rc-danger);
      font-size: 1.05rem;
    }

    .rcm-image-split {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 0.95fr 1.05fr;
      gap: 30px;
      align-items: center;
    }

    .rcm-image-card { position: relative; min-height: 430px; }

    .rcm-image-card img {
      position: absolute;
      object-fit: cover;
      display: block;
      border: 10px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.82);
      box-shadow: var(--rc-shadow);
      transition: transform 0.35s ease;
    }

    .rcm-image-card img:hover { transform: rotate(0deg) scale(1.03) !important; }

    .rcm-img-main {
      width: 78%;
      height: 340px;
      left: 0;
      top: 20px;
      border-radius: 42px;
      transform: rotate(-2deg);
    }

    .rcm-img-small {
      width: 52%;
      height: 230px;
      right: 0;
      bottom: 0;
      border-radius: 34px;
      transform: rotate(4deg);
      object-fit: contain !important;
      background: #fff9ef;
    }

    .rcm-prep {
      background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0), rgba(127, 155, 114, 0.09), rgba(255, 255, 255, 0));
    }

    .rcm-steps {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr));
      gap: 18px;
      margin-top: 28px;
    }

    .rcm-step {
      padding: 24px;
      border-radius: var(--rc-radius-xl);
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.86);
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.12);
      box-shadow: 0 16px 42px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.10);
    }

    .rcm-step b {
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      width: 48px;
      height: 48px;
      margin-bottom: 18px;
      border-radius: 50%;
      background: rgba(127, 155, 114, 0.15);
      color: var(--rc-sage-dark);
      font-size: 1.15rem;
    }

    .rcm-step h3 { margin: 0 0 8px; color: var(--rc-moss); font-size: 1.16rem; }
    .rcm-step p { margin: 0; color: var(--rc-muted); }

    .rcm-sidebar {
      position: sticky;
      top: 22px;
      display: grid;
      gap: 18px;
    }

    .rcm-side-card {
      padding: 22px;
      border-radius: 28px;
      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.12);
      box-shadow: 0 16px 42px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.10);
    }

    .rcm-side-card h2 {
      margin: 0 0 14px;
      color: var(--rc-moss);
      font-size: 1.18rem;
      line-height: 1.2;
    }

    .rcm-side-card ul {
      display: grid;
      gap: 10px;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      list-style: none;
    }

    .rcm-side-card a {
      display: block;
      padding: 11px 12px;
      border-radius: 16px;
      background: #fff9ef;
      color: var(--rc-sage-dark);
      font-weight: 850;
      transition: transform 0.2s ease, background 0.2s ease;
    }

    .rcm-side-card a:hover { transform: translateX(4px); background: #fff4d8; }

    .rcm-note {
      padding: 20px;
      border-radius: 24px;
      background: #ffffff;
      border-left: 6px solid var(--rc-gold);
      color: var(--rc-muted);
      box-shadow: 0 12px 32px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.08);
    }

    .rcm-note strong { color: var(--rc-moss); }

    .rcm-benefits-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr));
      gap: 18px;
      margin-top: 24px;
    }

    .rcm-benefit {
      padding: 22px;
      border-radius: 26px;
      background: #ffffff;
      border: 1px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.12);
      box-shadow: 0 14px 36px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.08);
    }

    .rcm-benefit h3 { margin: 0 0 8px; color: var(--rc-moss); font-size: 1.15rem; }
    .rcm-benefit p { margin: 0; color: var(--rc-muted); }

    .rcm-final { padding: 70px 0 42px; background: #fef4f0; }

    .rcm-final-box {
      padding: clamp(28px, 5vw, 52px);
      border-radius: 46px;
      background:
        linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(28, 48, 27, 0.92), rgba(58, 84, 49, 0.86)),
        url("/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Rabbitcare-mulberries.png");
      background-size: cover;
      background-position: center;
      color: #ffffff;
      box-shadow: var(--rc-shadow);
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    .rcm-final-box .rcm-pill,
    .rcm-final-box h2,
    .rcm-final-box p {
      color: #ffffff;
      text-shadow: 0 3px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35);
    }

    .rcm-final-box p {
      max-width: 780px;
      margin: 0 0 16px;
      font-size: 1.08rem;
    }

    .rcm-final-box .rcm-btn-secondary {
      background: #ffffff;
      color: #2f4a2e;
      border: 2px solid #ffffff;
      box-shadow: 0 16px 34px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.22);
      text-shadow: none;
    }

    .rcm-related {
      padding: 74px 0;
      background: #fff9ef;
      opacity: 1 !important;
      transform: none !important;
      animation: none !important;
    }

    .rcm-related,
    .rcm-related * {
      opacity: 1 !important;
      filter: none !important;
      text-shadow: none !important;
    }

    .rcm-related .rcm-section-header {
      padding: 30px;
      border-radius: 34px;
      background: #ffffff;
      border: 2px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.22);
      box-shadow: 0 20px 54px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.14);
    }

    .rcm-related .rcm-section-header .rcm-pill { color: #4e6b45 !important; }

    .rcm-related .rcm-section-header h2 {
      color: #243320 !important;
      opacity: 1 !important;
      text-shadow: none !important;
    }

    .rcm-related .rcm-section-header p {
      color: #332d26 !important;
      opacity: 1 !important;
      text-shadow: none !important;
      font-weight: 650;
    }

    .rcm-related-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr));
      gap: 18px;
      margin-top: 28px;
    }

    .rcm-related-card {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 92px 1fr;
      gap: 15px;
      padding: 16px;
      border-radius: 24px;
      background: #ffffff !important;
      border: 2px solid rgba(78, 107, 69, 0.22);
      box-shadow: 0 20px 50px rgba(64, 43, 28, 0.15);
      transition: transform 0.22s ease, background 0.22s ease;
    }

    .rcm-related-card:hover { transform: translateY(-5px); background: #fff; }

    .rcm-related-card img {
      width: 92px;
      height: 92px;
      max-width: 92px;
      max-height: 92px;

            <span class="rcm-pill">Rabbit food guide</span>
            <h2>Mulberries are a sweet, soft summer fruit that rabbits can enjoy</h2>
            <p>
              Mulberries are a relatively unusual fruit in the UK, but rabbit owners with access to a mulberry tree often wonder whether the berries are safe to share. The good news is that ripe fresh mulberries are not toxic to rabbits and can be offered as an occasional treat.
            </p>
            <p>
              Unlike gooseberries or cranberries, mulberries are naturally quite sweet and soft when fully ripe, which means many rabbits take to them readily. However, that sweetness is exactly why portions need to be kept small, too much sugary fruit can upset a rabbit's delicate digestive system.
            </p>
          </section>

          <section class="rcm-panel" id="safe">
            <span class="rcm-pill">Safe in small amounts</span>
            <h2>Are mulberries safe for rabbits?</h2>
            <p>
              Yes, fresh ripe mulberries are safe for most healthy adult rabbits when offered in small amounts. Both the flesh and the skin can be eaten. The deep colour of ripe mulberries, whether red, dark purple or black, is a natural sign of ripeness and does not indicate any harm.
            </p>
            <p>
              As with all fruit treats, mulberries should sit firmly alongside, never in place of, the hay, fresh water and leafy greens that make up the core of a healthy rabbit diet. Hay should account for around 80–90% of everything a rabbit eats each day.
            </p>
          </section>

          <h2>How many mulberries can rabbits eat?</h2>
          <p>
            Mulberries should only be offered in small portions. Two or three ripe mulberries once or twice a week is a sensible guide for most healthy adult rabbits. Because mulberries are soft and sweet, it is easy to overfeed them, many rabbits will happily eat far more than is good for them.
          </p>
          <p>
            Smaller or younger rabbits should receive even smaller amounts. If you are introducing mulberries for the first time, start with just one berry and monitor your rabbit over the following day before offering more.
          </p>

          <ul class="rcm-list">
            <li>Offer two or three ripe mulberries at a time, not a large handful.</li>
            <li>Feed mulberries once or twice a week at most.</li>
            <li>Start with a single berry when introducing them for the first time.</li>
            <li>Watch for changes in poo, appetite or behaviour after any new food.</li>

          <h2>Too many mulberries can upset digestion</h2>
          <p>
            Mulberries are sweet and very soft when fully ripe, which makes it easy to offer too many without realising. Unripe mulberries are also much more astringent and should never be fed to rabbits.
          </p>
        </div>

        <ul class="rcm-warning-list">
          <li>
            <strong>Never feed unripe mulberries</strong>
            Unripe mulberries are astringent and hard on the digestive system. Only use fully ripe, deeply coloured berries that are soft to the touch.
          </li>

          <li>
            <strong>Watch for loose stools</strong>
            Too much sugary fruit can cause soft caecotrophs or digestive upset. If this happens, remove the fruit and return fully to hay and leafy greens.
          </li>

          <li>
            <strong>No mulberry products</strong>
            Do not feed mulberry jam, mulberry juice, dried mulberries, mulberry wine or any processed product containing mulberries to rabbits.
          </li>
        </ul>

            Among the tarter berries in this series, mulberries stand out for being genuinely palatable to most rabbits without much hesitation. Their soft texture means they require no preparation beyond washing, and their rich flavour tends to go down well.
          </p>
          <p>
            They are only available fresh for a short summer window, usually July to August in the UK, so they are naturally a seasonal treat rather than something offered year-round. That built-in scarcity is actually a helpful reminder to keep portions small and infrequent.
          </p>

            <a class="rcm-btn rcm-btn-primary" href="/what-do-rabbits-eat">Read the full rabbit food guide</a>
            <a class="rcm-btn rcm-btn-secondary" href="/best-hay-for-rabbits">Read the hay guide</a>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="rcm-section rcm-prep rcm-reveal" id="prepare">
      <div class="rcm-wrap">
        <div class="rcm-section-header">
          <span class="rcm-pill">Simple preparation</span>
          <h2>How to prepare mulberries for rabbits</h2>
          <p>
            Mulberries need very little preparation, but a few simple steps make sure what you offer is clean, ripe and safe.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="rcm-steps">
          <article class="rcm-step">
            <b>1</b>
            <h3>Choose ripe berries</h3>
            <p>Only use fully ripe mulberries, deeply coloured, soft to the touch, and sweet smelling. Avoid hard, pale or unripe berries entirely.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-step">
            <b>2</b>
            <h3>Wash gently</h3>
            <p>Rinse mulberries carefully under cold water. They are very soft and bruise easily, handle them gently to avoid crushing.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-step">
            <b>3</b>
            <h3>Check for stalks</h3>
            <p>Remove any small stalks before feeding. The berry itself is the only part to offer, the stalk is tough and unnecessary.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-step">
            <b>4</b>
            <h3>Feed occasionally</h3>
            <p>Offer two or three mulberries at a time, no more than once or twice a week, and only during the fresh summer season.</p>
          </article>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="rcm-section rcm-reveal" id="benefits">
      <div class="rcm-wrap">
        <div class="rcm-section-header">
          <span class="rcm-pill">Treat benefits</span>
          <h2>Benefits and signs your rabbit enjoys mulberries</h2>
          <p>
            When offered in moderation, mulberries can be one of the more enjoyable summer treats for rabbits. Most take to them easily, which also makes them useful for gentle bonding.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div class="rcm-benefits-grid">
          <article class="rcm-benefit">
            <h3>Seasonal variety</h3>
            <p>Mulberries add a natural seasonal treat during the short summer window when they are available fresh.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-benefit">
            <h3>Small amounts of nutrients</h3>
            <p>Mulberries contain vitamins C and K plus antioxidants, though they should complement rather than replace leafy greens.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-benefit">
            <h3>Easy to portion</h3>
            <p>Individual berries make mulberries straightforward to count and portion accurately for each serving.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-benefit">
            <h3>Bonding treat</h3>
            <p>Because most rabbits enjoy the sweet flavour, mulberries can work well as a treat during gentle handling or positive interaction.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-benefit">
            <h3>Signs they enjoy it</h3>
            <p>Your rabbit may approach quickly, pick up the berry eagerly, chew enthusiastically or look around for more immediately after finishing.</p>
          </article>

          <article class="rcm-benefit">
            <h3>Still limit treats</h3>
            <p>Even a rabbit that clearly loves mulberries should only have them occasionally to keep their overall diet properly balanced.</p>
          </article>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>



    <section class="rcm-section rcm-faq rcm-reveal" id="faqs" aria-label="Rabbit mulberry FAQs">
      <div class="rcm-narrow">
        <div class="rcm-section-header">
          <span class="rcm-pill">Frequently asked questions</span>
          <h2>Mulberry FAQs</h2>
          <p>Quick answers to common questions about feeding mulberries to rabbits.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="rcm-faq-list">
          <details class="rcm-faq-item">
            <summary>Can rabbits eat mulberries safely?</summary>
            <p>Yes, rabbits can eat fresh ripe mulberries in small amounts. They should be an occasional treat rather than a daily food because they are naturally sweet.</p>
          </details>

          <details class="rcm-faq-item">
            <summary>How many mulberries can a rabbit eat?</summary>
            <p>For most healthy adult rabbits, two or three ripe mulberries once or twice a week is a sensible maximum. Start with one berry when introducing them for the first time.</p>
          </details>

          <details class="rcm-faq-item">
            <summary>Can rabbits eat unripe mulberries?</summary>
            <p>No. Unripe mulberries are more astringent and harder on a rabbit's digestive system. Only feed fully ripe, soft, deeply coloured mulberries.</p>
          </details>

          <details class="rcm-faq-item">
            <summary>Can rabbits eat dried mulberries?</summary>
            <p>No. Dried mulberries are concentrated in sugar and are not a suitable rabbit treat. Stick to fresh ripe mulberries only.</p>
          </details>

          <details class="rcm-faq-item">
            <summary>Do mulberries replace hay for rabbits?</summary>
            <p>No. Mulberries are only a small treat. Hay should remain the main part of a rabbit's diet, with leafy greens and fresh water available every day.</p>
          </details>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section class="rcm-final rcm-reveal">
      <div class="rcm-wrap rcm-final-box">
        <span class="rcm-pill">Final thoughts</span>
        <h2>Mulberries can be a safe and enjoyable summer treat for rabbits</h2>
        <p>
          Rabbits can eat fresh ripe mulberries in small amounts, and unlike some of the more astringent berries, most rabbits find them genuinely appealing. Their short summer season in the UK means they are naturally an occasional treat rather than something to worry about offering year-round.
        </p>
        <p>
          Always use fully ripe, freshly washed mulberries, remove any stalks, and keep portions to two or three berries at a time. Never feed unripe, dried or processed mulberry products. As always, hay should form the foundation of your rabbit's daily diet, with leafy greens and vegetables making up the rest.
        </p>
